text: It can be unjust when the courts limit the liability of those who commit breaches of contract.
Examine the rules of causation and remoteness applied by the courts and critically assess the
extent to which you agree with the statement above. [25]
The doctrine of promissory estoppel has resolved the hardship frequently experienced as a result
of applying the Common Law rules of consideration.
Discuss the circumstances under which this doctrine is applied and critically analyse its
effectiveness in mitigating the potential harshness of the Common Law. [25]
Explain and critically evaluate the rules for the incorporation of exemption clauses into a contract.
Section B
Pablo is a professional racing driver. Q Racing employs him for the season to drive for its team.
Pablo signs a contract with Q Racing; its terms state that while working for the company, he
must not drive professionally for any other motor racing team. He does not read the terms of the
contract.
Several months later, Q Racing discovers that Pablo has been racing for T Sport. Q Racing wants
to enforce its contract with Pablo and prevent him from driving for T Sport until the current season
is over.
Discuss whether or not Pablo is bound by his contract with Q Racing and consider the likelihood
of an award of any of the remedies that might be sought. [25]
Sukhi takes her dog, Fifi, for a walk in the local park one day in April. She lets the dog off the lead
and Fifi runs off, chasing a rabbit. After half an hour of searching for Fifi, Sukhi returns home. The
following day, Sukhi places an advertisement in the local newspaper offering £500 for the return of
Fifi.
A few days later,Tatiana is on her way home from work and finds a dog that appears to be lost.
She checks the dog’s collar and finds a tag bearing the name Fifi and giving Sukhi’s address.
Tatiana takes the dog to the address and knocks on the door. Sukhi is delighted to be reunited
with Fifi and thanks Tatiana.
On her way home, Tatiana buys a copy of the local newspaper and sees the advertisement placed
by Sukhi.
Advise Sukhi and Tatiana as to their contractual rights and obligations in this situation. [25]
Ursula, Veena and Wanda have worked together for many years. None of them earns very much
and they decide to buy tickets together to enter the National Lottery in order to win a large sum of
money so that they can all give up working.
They agree that each will contribute £2, that £6 worth of lottery tickets will be purchased each
week and that any winnings will be shared equally between them. They also agree to take it in
turns to purchase the tickets.
After several months, one of their tickets, purchased that week by Wanda, wins £500 000 in the
lottery draw on a Saturday. Ursula and Veena arrive at work on the following Monday morning,
only to discover that Wanda is not there. They discover that Wanda has claimed the prize money
for herself and is not going to share any of it with them.
Advise Wanda as to her legal entitlement to keep all of the winnings in this situation and explore
any remedies that Ursula and Veena might pursue against her. [25]
